title: The Classical Tradition I
description: The first in a two-quarter sequence providing foundational knowledge and skills through engaging with the European classical tradition in music.

title: The Classical Tradition II
description: The second in a two-quarter sequence providing foundational knowledge and skills through engaging with the European classical tradition in music.

title: History of European Music: From the Renaissance through the Baroque
description: An introduction to the analysis of musical styles and forms, to the sources for constructing music history and reconstructing historical music, and to J.S. Bach.
prerequisites_raw: MUSIC 16C with a minimum grade of C-

title: History of European Music: Hasse to Mahler
description: An introduction to the analysis of musical styles and forms, and to the sources for constructing music history and reconstructing historical music, to Richard Wagner.
prerequisites_raw: MUSIC 40B with a minimum grade of D. Recommended: MUSIC 16D

title: 20th Century Music
description: Survey of principal composers, movements, and compositional techniques of Western art music of the modern era.
prerequisites_raw: MUSIC 16C with a minimum grade of C-

title: Major Composer
description: Study of the works of an important composer with emphasis on their significance in historical and social contexts. Composers selected represent a wide variety of historical periods, nationalities, and stylistic orientations.

title: History of Film Music
description: Course provides an overview of film music history. Special emphasis will be placed on developing an analytic vocabulary for musical elements and cultivating an understanding of how music can function within a film.

title: Music in Multimedia
description: Students explore intersections between music and other media forms through creating multimedia projects, readings, lectures, and discussion. Students produce music, edit video, increase media literacy, and study theories behind how music communicates meaning.

title: Introductory Topics in Music Technology
description: Introductory topics in electronic music, digital audio, and other aspects of music technology.

title: Introductory Topics in Music and Culture
description: Examines music and musical practices in different historical periods, societies, and cultural settings.

title: History of Hip Hop
description: Surveys the history of hip hop music from its origins to the present day.

title: Introduction to Music Technology
description: A study of the influence of technology on the musical culture and aesthetics from the 20th century to the present. Work includes lectures, readings, listenings, discussions, demonstrations, writing, and experimentation.

title: Piano for Music Majors
description: Private weekly lessons. Materials Fee

title: Strings for Music Majors
description: Private weekly lessons. Materials Fee

title: Guitar, Lute, and Other Plucked Instruments for Music Majors
description: Private weekly lessons. Materials Fee

title: History of Jazz
description: Development of jazz from African and African American folk origins through blues, early jazz, swing, bebop, "cool" jazz, fusion, free jazz, and contemporary trends.

title: Experiments in Music
description: Scientists explain the cognition of music using experimental methodology; artists expand the domain of music by trying previously unknown ways of making it. These two types of experiment deepen our understanding of music, from both scientific and artistic vantage points.

title: MAHUR-Pish Radif: Introduction to Classical Persian Music
description: Survey of art music in Iran and basic structures of classical Persian music, with emphasis on MAHUR modal system and different instruments of classical Persian music. No musical experience required, but interest in vocal music is strongly recommended.

title: HOMAYUN-Pish Radif: Introduction to Classical Persian Music
description: Survey of art music in Iran and basic structures of classical Persian music, with emphasis on HOMAYUN modal system and famous musicians and performers of classical Persian music. No musical experience required, but interest in vocal music is strongly recommended.

title: SHUR-Pish Radif: Introduction to Classical Persian Music
description: Survey of art music in Iran and basic structures of classical Persian music, with emphasis on the SHUR modal system and different poetic rhythms in classical Persian music. No musical experience required, but interest in vocal music is strongly recommended.

title: Piano Literature
description: Survey of stringed keyboard literature from the English Virginalists through twentieth-century composers. Historical, formal, and stylistic considerations of music presented. Performances by class participants and occasional outside guests.
prerequisites_raw: MUSIC 16A and MUSIC 16B and MUSIC 16C

title: Piano Literature
description: Survey of stringed keyboard literature from the English Virginalists through twentieth-century composers. Historical, formal, and stylistic considerations of music presented. Performances by class participants and occasional outside guests.
prerequisites_raw: MUSIC 16A and MUSIC 16B and MUSIC 16C

description: Survey of stringed keyboard literature from the English Virginalists through twentieth-century composers. Historical, formal, and stylistic considerations of music presented. Performances by class participants and occasional outside guests.
prerequisites_raw: MUSIC 16A and MUSIC 16B and MUSIC 16C

title: Piano Pedagogy
description: The materials and methods of piano instruction are examined and evaluated.

title: Post-Tonal Theory
description: Significant harmonic, rhythmic, and structural practices since 1900. Analysis and written work exploring free atonality and serialism; neo-tonal practices such as use of extended tertian harmonies, modalism, pandiatonicism, and non-tertian harmonies; structural principles such as aleatory, metric modulation and minimalism.
prerequisites_raw: MUSIC 16D

title: Jazz Theory
description: Study of jazz harmony and melody construction in improvisation. Covered topics include terminology, chord symbols, notation, voicings, and scales as commonly used in jazz and popular music. Issues regarding tonality and ramifications of the blue scale are also examined.
prerequisites_raw: MUSIC 16D

title: Instrumentation
description: Ranges and capabilities of modern orchestral instruments. Exercise in writing for various combinations of wind, string, and percussion instruments and for full orchestra.
prerequisites_raw: MUSIC 16C

title: Topics in Medieval Music
description: Topics in medieval music.
prerequisites_raw: MUSIC 39A and MUSIC 39B . Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

description: Topics in renaissance music.

description: Topics in classical music.

description: Topics in 20th century music.

description: Topics in Jazz Music.

title: Studies in Ethnomusicology
description: Topics in Ethnomusicology.

title: Studies in Music History
description: Specialized topics in musical genres; culture and social issues; performance practices; and interrelated arts.
prerequisites_raw: MUSIC 39A and MUSIC 39B . Satisfactory completion of the lower-division writing requirement

title: Composition
description: Exercises and projects for diverse instrumental-vocal combinations; contemporary techniques and problems. Participation in the improvisation ensemble and working with electronic media.
prerequisites_raw: MUSIC 16C

title: Computer Music Composition
description: Exercises in the composition of music uniquely possible by computer, including digital signal processing, computer control of synthesizers and processors, and algorithmic composition. Demonstrations and musical analyses in class; considerable studio work outside class.
prerequisites_raw: MUSIC 51

title: Counterpoint
description: Studies in contrapuntal practices of various style periods such as the 16th, 18th, and 20th centuries.
prerequisites_raw: MUSIC 16B with a minimum grade of C-

title: Analysis
description: Methods of formal analysis applicable to all Western musical styles: additive, continuous, transformational, and hierarchic forms; rhythm, texture, and sonority as form and process.
prerequisites_raw: MUSIC 16D

title: Song Literature
description: A survey of song literature. Designed as an overview of the song repertoire, German Lieder.

title: Song Literature
description: A survey of song literature. Designed as an overview of the song repertoire, French mélodie.

title: Advanced Study in Composition
description: Individual weekly lessons in composition.
prerequisites_raw: MUSIC 150 with a minimum grade of C-

title: Diction
description: In-depth study of the International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA), including its transcription and pronunciation, and its application for singers. Introduction to IPA and Italian diction.

title: Diction
description: In-depth study of the International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA), including its transcription and pronunciation, and its application for singers. German diction.
prerequisites_raw: MUSIC 158A

title: Diction
description: In-depth study of the International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA), including its transcription and pronunciation, and its application for singers. French Diction.
prerequisites_raw: MUSIC 158A and MUSIC 158B

title: University Orchestra
description: Study and performance of standard orchestral repertory and works by contemporary composers. Membership is open to all qualified students by audition only.
prerequisites_raw: Audition required

title: Wind Ensemble
description: Study and performance of works written for varying combinations of wind and percussion instruments. Membership is open to all qualified students by audition only.
prerequisites_raw: Audition required

title: University Chorus
description: Make-up of the ensembles varies and may include University Chorus, Chamber Choir, Madrigal Singers, Women's Chorus, and Reading Choir. Membership is open to all students.

title: University Chorus: Accompanying
description: Keyboard accompanying for one of the UCI choral organizations, with individual coaching in sight reading, score reading, and other accompanying skills.

title: Opera Workshop
description: Preparation and performance of operatic repertoire, including arias, scenes, and fully staged operas, and/or stage training and role analysis.

title: Opera Workshop: Accompanying
description: Training in techniques and operatic repertory for keyboard players.

title: Piano for Music Performance Majors
description: Private weekly lessons. Materials Fee

title: Strings for Music Performance Majors
description: Private weekly lessons. Materials Fee

title: String Accompaniment
description: Chamber ensemble experience with the solo string repertory for keyboard, participation in the weekly string master class, performance in public recitals.

title: Winds for Music Performance Majors
description: Private weekly lessons. Materials Fee

title: Voice for Music Performance Majors
description: Private weekly lessons. Materials Fee

title: Percussion for Music Performance Majors
description: Private weekly lessons. Materials Fee

title: Guitar, Lute, and Other Plucked Instruments for Music Performance Majors
description: Private weekly lessons and a weekly master class/workshop for the discussion of solo repertory and performance practice, including special topics such as historical notational systems, traditional American guitar styles, and demonstrations of period plucked instruments. Materials Fee

title: Chamber Singers
description: A select ensemble specializing in vocal chamber music from all periods. Frequent performances on and off campus. Membership is open to all singers by audition. Materials Fee

title: Chamber Ensembles
description: Make-up of the ensembles varies and may include various Classical ensembles, Latin Jazz Ensemble, Small Jazz Combos, Percussion Ensemble, and Guitar Ensemble. Membership is open to all qualified students by audition only.

title: Jazz Orchestra
description: Rehearsal and performance of literature written for large jazz ensemble with emphasis on methods and materials. Laboratory setting for new arrangers and/or composers of modern jazz pieces.

title: Improvisation
description: Improvisation has been central to all music traditions. Course explores real-time music-making in a variety of non-notated contexts. Different improvisational styles are presented, including jazz, Asian improvisation, and experimental modern music. Emphasis on actual classroom performance.

title: Advanced Jazz Combo
description: Small-group jazz ensemble and improvisational workshop. Range of music covered encompasses the full traditional jazz from improvised ragtime up through the most current avant-garde musical techniques.

title: Jazz Composition I
description: Performance and lecture course for writing and performing original jazz compositions. Emphasis is placed on composing as a way to create new improvisational frameworks. Cyclical forms, modal compositions, blues-oriented compositions, and ballad writing.
prerequisites_raw: MUSIC 78 and MUSIC 132

title: Jazz Composition II
description: Performance and lecture course for writing and performing original jazz compositions. Emphasis is placed on composing as a way to create new improvisational frameworks. Non-functional harmony, contemporary forms, free-bop, and current trends.
prerequisites_raw: MUSIC 78 and MUSIC 132 and MUSIC 183A

title: Jazz Composition III
description: Performance and lecture course for writing and performing original jazz compositions. Emphasis is placed on composing as a way to create new improvisational frameworks. Study of modern tonal-center compositions, intervallic compositions, and alternate rhythms.
prerequisites_raw: MUSIC 78 and MUSIC 132 and MUSIC 183A and MUSIC 183B

title: Integrated Composition, Improvisation, and Technology Workshop
description: A practice-based course in which students create original musical works through composition, improvisation, and/or technology, both individually and collaboratively.
prerequisites_raw: MUSIC 16C

title: Accompanying for Plucked Strings: Continuo and Changes
description: Students apply theory to their instruments as they learn the basics of pre-1800 continuo playing and post-1900 jazz charts. Includes discussions of appropriate repertory, treatment of harmonic progressions, and finer points of style and technique.
prerequisites_raw: MUSIC 16C

title: Tutorial in Music
description: Supplemental instruction related to student's area of study. Taken only when the materials studied lie outside regular departmental offerings, and when the student has no formal chance to pursue the subject.
prerequisites_raw: Undergraduate advisor approval required

title: Conducting
description: Introduces students to the basic techniques employed in the practice of conducting and includes score study and development of leadership skills.
prerequisites_raw: MUSIC 16D and MUSIC 40B and MUSIC 40C

title: Senior Thesis
description: With consultation in regularly scheduled meetings, students identify and study relevant texts and materials and prepare a prospectus for an original thesis.
prerequisites_raw: Senior standing in the Honors Program in Music and Culture

title: Senior Thesis
description: Students submit an outline and preliminary drafts of section of their thesis to the instructor, on a schedule supervised by the instructor. The final version will address the instructor's comments and criticisms.
prerequisites_raw: MUSIC 195A

title: Word and Music
description: Performance class for advanced singers and pianists with emphasis on collaborative approach to vocal literature.

title: Independent Study
description: Student-devised research/composition project, with faculty guidance, resulting in a formal paper/project. Taken only when materials studied lie outside regular departmental offerings or when students have no formal chance to pursue the subject.
prerequisites_raw: Undergraduate or graduate advisor approval required

title: Bibliography and Research
description: Required of all entering students. A systematic introduction to the bibliographical tools both in the general field of music and in the student's areas of specialization.

title: Proseminar in Musicology
description: Introduces significant issues and recent developments in musicology and music criticism, including exposure to the controversies that have brought change and reflection to the discipline.
prerequisites_raw: MUSIC 200 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of B

title: Music Thesis
description: Intensive work dedicated to researching and writing a Master's thesis under the supervision of a faculty advisor.
prerequisites_raw: MUSIC 200 with a minimum grade of B

title: Proseminar in Music Theory and Analysis
description: Introduction to music theories, analytic approaches, and methodologies as applied to repertories drawn from Western art and popular music.
prerequisites_raw: MUSIC 200 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of B

title: Seminar in Creative Practices
description: Core first-year seminar required for graduate students in the Integrated Composition, Improvisation, and Technology emphasis of the M.A. and Ph.D. programs. Composition and presentation of original student works, lecture, and discussion.

title: Choral Conducting
description: Intensive private instruction and study of the various choral literatures.

title: Performance
description: Contents vary according to the student's major instrument. Intensive private instruction and study of the various literatures.

title: Composition
description: Intensive work in composition geared to each student's level of competence.

title: Graduate Recital
description: Performance of public recital.

title: Computer Music Composition and Production
description: Study of the composition and production of music made uniquely possible by the computer, including usage of prevalent digital music technology, techniques of digital signal processing, and computer control of synthesizers and audio processors.

title: Seminar in Musicology
description: Focuses on current scholarship in musicology and related fields with a strong critical content. Addresses topics relative to their historical and stylistic periods. Recent topics have included Stravinsky, Holy Women, Mahler, Historiography, Issues in Performance Practice, and Brahms’s Chamber Music.
prerequisites_raw: MUSIC 200 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of B

title: Seminar in Music Theory and Analysis
description: Typical topics include Schenkerian theory and analysis, contemporary form theory, and advanced techniques in the analysis of late 19th-century and contemporary music (e.g., transformational theory, Neo-Riemannian, and scale network theory).
prerequisites_raw: MUSIC 200 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of B

title: Improvisation
description: Introduces the practice and history of improvisation in diverse fields of Western music since 1950. Performance projects and group critiques, weekly reading and listening assignments, participation in a class concert, and a research paper.

title: Critical Studies in Music
description: A critical examination of music traditions, institutions, and aesthetics, employing new scholarship in music and new critical studies in other disciplines.
prerequisites_raw: MUSIC 200 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of B

title: Theoretical ICIT Seminar
description: Seminar studying new genres and topics that integrate composition, improvisation, new technologies, and non-classical cultures.

title: Practical ICIT Seminar
description: Study of new practices and techniques that integrate composition, improvisation, new technologies, and non-classical cultures.

title: Thesis Colloquium
description: ICIT students present their thesis work-in-progress for discussion and criticism. Faculty and visiting artists/scholars also present their current work.

title: Graduate Projects
description: Substantial projects in performance, conducting, or composition (other than those specifically required for the degree), accompanied by a summary paper.

title: First-Year Research and Writing Seminar I
description: Guided reading for one quarter on a broad subject selected by the instructor, followed by one quarter in which the student undertakes independent research on the selected topic, leading to a substantial term paper.
prerequisites_raw: MUSIC 200 with a minimum grade of B

title: First-Year Research and Writing Seminar II
description: Guided reading for one quarter on a broad subject selected by the instructor, followed by one quarter in which the student undertakes independent research on the selected topic, leading to a substantial term paper.
prerequisites_raw: MUSIC 200 with a minimum grade of B and MUSIC 242A with a minimum grade of B

title: Second-Year Research and Writing Tutorial I
description: In this two-quarter sequence, students gain expertise in a first area of research concentration by undertaking directed reading on a topic of their choice and then writing a paper of near-publishable length and quality on that topic.
prerequisites_raw: MUSIC 242B with a minimum grade of B

title: Second-Year Research and Writing Tutorial II
description: In this two-quarter sequence, students gain expertise in a first area of research concentration by undertaking directed reading on a topic of their choice and then writing a paper of near-publishable length and quality on that topic.
prerequisites_raw: MUSIC 243A with a minimum grade of B

title: Readings for the Qualifying Examination
description: Directed reading in preparation for the Qualifying Examination.
prerequisites_raw: MUSIC 243B with a minimum grade of B

title: Prospectus Research
description: Research and writing of the Dissertation Prospectus.
prerequisites_raw: MUSIC 244 with a minimum grade of B

title: Directed Research
description: Preparation for qualifying exams in ICIT or an individual research project, resulting in a substantial paper or comparable documentation of the research results.

title: Contemporary Ensemble
description: Chamber ensemble for the performance of contemporary music, including newly composed and improvised forms.

title: Dissertation Research
description: Research and writing of a Ph.D. dissertation.

title: Independent Study
description: Student-devised research/composition project, with faculty guidance, resulting in a formal paper/project. Taken only when materials studied lie outside regular departmental offerings or when students have no formal chance to pursue the subject.
prerequisites_raw: Graduate advisor approval required

title: Research in Neurobiology and Behavior
description: Individual research with Neurobiology and Behavior faculty.

title: Research in Neurobiology and Behavior
description: Individual research with Neurobiology and Behavior faculty.
prerequisites_raw: NEURBIO 200A with a minimum grade of B-

title: Research in Neurobiology and Behavior
description: Individual research with Neurobiology and Behavior faculty.
prerequisites_raw: NEURBIO 200B with a minimum grade of B-

title: Research in Neurobiology and Behavior
description: Individual research with Neurobiology and Behavior faculty.

title: Research in Neurobiology and Behavior
description: Individual research with Neurobiology and Behavior faculty.
prerequisites_raw: NEURBIO 201A with a minimum grade of B-

title: Research in Neurobiology and Behavior
description: Individual research with Neurobiology and Behavior faculty.
prerequisites_raw: NEURBIO 201B with a minimum grade of B-

title: Foundations of Neuroscience
description: Intended to expose students to critical reading and analysis of the primary neuroscience literature. Instructors from departments associated with the Interdepartmental Neuroscience Program participate and discuss topics of current interest.

title: Foundations of Neuroscience
description: Intended to expose students to critical reading and analysis of the primary neuroscience literature. Instructors from departments associated with the Interdepartmental Neuroscience Program participate and discuss topics of current interest.
prerequisites_raw: NEURBIO 202A with a minimum grade of B-

title: Molecular Neuroscience
description: Surveys molecular and cellular mechanisms involved in neuronal function, including control of gene expression, post-transcriptional and post-translational processing, RNA and protein targeting, cell death mechanisms, and molecular genetic basis of neurological disorders. Overview of the molecular aspects of developmental neurobiology.

title: Cellular Neuroscience
description: Neurophysiological and neurochemical mechanisms of electrical and chemical signaling in neurons. Topics include generation of resting- and action-potentials, voltage- and ligand-gated ion channels, second messenger systems, and synaptic transmission and integration.

title: Systems Neuroscience
description: Study of the mammalian nervous system at the systems level. Anatomy and physiology of sensory, motor, and integrative functions.

title: Behavioral Neuroscience
description: Overview of fundamental conceptual and experimental issues in the neurobiology of learning and memory. The approach is a cross-level integration of research in molecular-genetic, cellular, circuit, systems, and behavioral analyses.

title: Foundations in Neuroimmunology II
description: The immune system supports normal brain development as well as controls central nervous system (CNS) infection, and neurodegenerative and neurological diseases. Assesses how the immune system contributes to both host defense and disease.
prerequisites_raw: Undergraduate- or graduate-level immunology experience is required

title: Neural Coding, Computation, and Dynamics
description: Theoretical principles and biological mechanisms underlying how brains acquire, assimilate, store, and retrieve information, compute adaptive responses to external inputs, and how knowledge is extracted from experience to generate an internal model of the world.
prerequisites_raw: At least one upper-division course in the field of Neuroscience or one upper-division course in Cognitive Science or Machine Learning

title: Bioinformatics and Systems Biology
description: Students learn the fundamentals of bioinformatics, genomic approaches, and Linux and R program in order to analyze RNA-sequencing data.

title: Epigenetics in Health and Disease
description: Focuses on the role of chromatin/nuclear structure organization (histone and DNA modification, chromatin remodeling, higher order chromatin structure and nuclear organization) on gene regulation, DNA replication and repair, relevant to development, metabolism, learning and memory, and human disease.
prerequisites_raw: MOL BIO 203 with a minimum grade of B- or MOL BIO 204 with a minimum grade of B- or NEURBIO 206 with a minimum grade of B-

title: Neurobiology of Drug Addiction
description: Provides a comprehensive overview of topics in the addiction field, including drug pharmacology, models/approaches to investigate addiction, brain circuits, genetics, epigenetics, and the cellular and molecular biology of drug addiction.

title: Cortex: Structure, Function, and Plasticity
description: Structured to include lectures and presentation of papers about cortex with emphasis on sensory-motor cortex. Both historical and current perspectives on cortical structure-function relationship are critically evaluated.

title: Neurobiology of Aging and Alzheimer's Disease
description: Outlines changes occurring in aging and Alzheimer’s disease, and clinical manifestations of those changes. Emphasis on genetic and lifestyle risk factors, molecular mechanisms that are basis for detrimental and protective responses, diagnosis, and developing therapies for aging and Alzheimer's disease.
prerequisites_raw: NEURBIO 209 with a minimum grade of B-

title: Functional Imaging of the Nervous System
description: Overview of technical and applied aspects of imaging techniques available for studying the nervous system. The areas emphasized are cellular and subcellular imaging of neural function, systems-level imaging of brain function, and imaging of the human brain.

title: Advanced Analysis of Learning and Memory
description: Advanced analysis of contemporary research concerning the nature and neurobiological bases of learning and memory. Special emphasis is given to time-dependent processes involved in memory storage.

title: Programming for Neuroscience Research
description: A neuroscience-specific introduction to programming and data analysis using either MATLAB or Scientific PYTHON. Students will learn general programming skills and effective use of programming for data management, statistical analysis, and image analysis.

title: Statistics and Experimental Design
description: Introduction to common methods for statistical analysis used in neurobiology. Topics covered include t-tests, ANOVAs, correlations and regressions, general linear model, power analysis, and non-parametric tests.

title: Auditory Neuroscience
description: Multidisciplinary overview of brain mechanisms of hearing. Emphasizes breadth of auditory function and research: single neurons to psychoacoustics, the chochlea to the cortex, and basic science to clinic.

title: Colloquium in Neurobiology and Behavior
description: Presentation of contemporary research problems in neurobiology and behavior and related areas by invited speakers.

title: Neuroscience Journal Club
description: Covers emerging topics in addiction neuroscience research in a journal club format. Students discuss recent articles and may present an article of their choosing. Students gain skills in critical thinking and scientific communication.

title: Nutrition Across the Lifespan
description: Focuses on the relationship between diet and health, and how the human body responds to different diets and food components. Emphasizes how diet interacts with activity and the impact of exercise or sedentary lifestyle on health.

title: Introduction to Pain Medicine
description: Gives students introductory knowledge in pain medicine.

title: Compassion in Health Care
description: An overview of the importance of compassion in health care, providing examples from a variety of health care professions through lectures and discussion.

title: Introduction to Nursing Informatics
description: Covers topics relevant to evidence-based practice; nursing informatics as a specialty; electronic health records and clinical informatics; clinical decision support and decision analysis; using informatics to promote community/population health; telenursing and remote access telehealth; and ethical issues in nursing informatics.

title: Frameworks for Professional Nursing Practice
description: Conceptual frameworks for professional practice. Scope of professional nursing, jurisprudence and ethics, professional interpersonal relationships, and health care delivery systems in the context of the social, political, and economic environments. Socialization of the student for professional roles in nursing.
prerequisites_raw: BIO SCI D170 with a minimum grade of C and PHRMSCI 120 with a minimum grade of C and PHRMSCI 120L with a minimum grade of C and BIO SCI M115 with a minimum grade of C. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Physical Assessment
description: Development of skills in communication, interviewing, functional and physical health assessment across the life-span, the art and science of human care, and clinical judgment. Provides in-depth introductory review/synthesis of physical assessment skills and knowledge covering the life-span. Materials Fee
prerequisites_raw: BIO SCI M115 with a minimum grade of C and BIO SCI D170 with a minimum grade of C and PHRMSCI 120 with a minimum grade of C and PHRMSCI 120L with a minimum grade of C

title: Nursing Skills
description: Provides an in-depth introductory review and synthesis of physical assessment skills covering the lifespan, application of the nursing process, nursing interventions, nursing evaluations, patient care management, and the development of critical thinking in nursing practice.
prerequisites_raw: NUR SCI 109A with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 108W with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 119 with a minimum grade of C

title: Human Growth and Development through the Lifespan
description: Examines theories and concepts of typical human development throughout the life cycle, from the time of conception through adulthood, and familiarizes students with the many forces that shape individual development, including family, society, and culture.
prerequisites_raw: COGS 7A with a minimum grade of C or PSCI 9 with a minimum grade of C

title: Applied Pharmacology
description: Presents principles of pharmacology applied to interventions in pathophysiologic states across the life span. Discussion of the major drug groups with implications for monitoring, drug administration, toxicity, and patient education are included.
prerequisites_raw: NUR SCI 108W with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 109A with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 119 with a minimum grade of C

title: Pathophysiology
description: Presents content on pathologic alterations in physiologic processes in cells, tissues, organs, and systems across the life span. Emphasis on critical thinking, application of concepts to clinical practice, and related research.
prerequisites_raw: BIO SCI M115 with a minimum grade of C and BIO SCI D170 with a minimum grade of C and PHRMSCI 120 with a minimum grade of C and PHRMSCI 120L with a minimum grade of C

title: Medical Surgical Nursing I
description: Introduction to medical surgical nursing application focused on the older adult population. Students assess, interpret, and provide priority nursing interventions with an emphasis the unique factors influencing nursing management of older adults.
prerequisites_raw: NUR SCI 108W with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 109A with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 119 with a minimum grade of C

title: Medical Surgical Nursing II
description: Examines nursing assessment and advanced nursing management for acute and chronic health problems within the inpatient hospital setting. Emphasizes assessment, health history, diagnostic reasoning and nursing prioritization of care in medically complicated patients.
prerequisites_raw: NUR SCI 109B with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 117 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 121A with a minimum grade of C

title: Research Methods and Applications in Health Care
description: Foundational concepts of research in health care. Emphasizes critical evaluation and interpretation of research for application in practice.
prerequisites_raw: STATS 7 with a minimum grade of C or STATS 8 with a minimum grade of C or SOCIOL 10A with a minimum grade of C or SOC SCI 10A with a minimum grade of C or COGS 10A with a minimum grade of C. Satisfactory completion of Lower-Division Writing requirement is recommended

title: Human Behavior and Mental Health Care
description: Biopsychosocial and cultural influences on promotion and restoration of mental health in adults and adolescents. Assessment, classification, and care of clients with mental health problems and/or substance abuse. Concurrent practicum in adult/adolescent inpatient psychiatric units and outpatient mental health clinics.
prerequisites_raw: NUR SCI 109B with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 117 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 121A with a minimum grade of C

title: Complementary and Integrative Health
description: Complementary and integrative healthcare emphasized a holistic, patient-focused approach to healthcare and wellness. Key research is critically evaluated and applications for improving patient care emphasized. Knowledge and skills are developed through lectures, guest speakers, and discussion.

title: Personal and Social Resilience in the Age of the Climate Crisis
description: In our rapidly changing world, many climate and other interrelated global crises are undermining human well-being. Students gain invaluable personal and social resilience skills (e.g., mindfulness), and implement collaborative high impact projects to navigate and build a meaningful future.

title: Community-Based Health Care
description: Epidemiology, primary health care promotion, and disease prevention applied to nursing care of individuals, families, groups, and communities. Includes sociocultural, political, economic, and environmental influences. Concepts and methods of assessing populations and communities incorporated in concurrent practicum.
prerequisites_raw: NUR SCI 174 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 176 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 179AW with a minimum grade of C

title: Pediatrics: Care of Children and Families
description: Provides didactic and clinical experiences in nursing management of infants, children, and adolescents with acute, chronic and/or life-threatening conditions. Incorporates concepts of family-centered care, teamwork and collaboration, patient safety, quality improvement and informatics, utilizing an evidence-based practice approach.
prerequisites_raw: NUR SCI 101 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 116 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 121B with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 128 with a minimum grade of C

title: Maternity and Women’s Health Care
description: Provides didactic and clinical experiences in nursing management of women’s wellness across the lifespan, the childbirth process, and newborn care. Incorporates concepts of family-centered care, teamwork and collaboration, patient safety, quality improvement and informatics, utilizing an evidence-based practice approach.
prerequisites_raw: NUR SCI 101 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 116 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 121B with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 128 with a minimum grade of C

title: Critical and Specialty Health Care
description: Delivery of patient-centered care for individuals with life-threatening alterations in health status utilizing technology and pharmacology for life support. Concurrent practicum in critical care units emphasizes collaboration, team work, and quality improvement in safe care delivery.
prerequisites_raw: NUR SCI 172 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 173 with a minimum grade of C

title: Clinical Preceptorship
description: Focuses on in-depth clinical nursing practice and preparation for transition to independent practice. Students are mentored by a preceptor who is an expert clinician in the clinical area and guided through critical thinking and clinical decision-making exercises.
prerequisites_raw: NUR SCI 174 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 176 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 179AW with a minimum grade of C

title: Leadership and Management in Health Care
description: Principles, concepts, and theories related to organizations, management, leadership, decision-making, and group process applied to the delivery of health care. The professional nurse using evidenced-based practice, collaboration, and informatics is incorporated in concurrent practicum emphasizing safe patient care delivery.
prerequisites_raw: NUR SCI 172 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 173 with a minimum grade of C

title: Scholarly Concentration I
description: Focuses on analysis and use of evidence to improve nursing practice. Emphasis is to develop critical analysis skills synthesizing a body of research evidence for clinical issues on a formal, collaborative written paper.
prerequisites_raw: NUR SCI 172 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 173 with a minimum grade of C

title: Scholarly Concentration II
description: Continuation of evidence-based research and application for nursing practice. Emphasis is to develop a collaborative quality improvement project with clinical nurses applying the evidence to improve nursing practice.
prerequisites_raw: NUR SCI 174 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 176 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 179AW with a minimum grade of C

title: Independent Study in Nursing Science
description: Original research with Nursing Science faculty.

title: Research Methods and Evaluation for Evidence-Based Practice
description: Equips students with the essential knowledge and skills to understand, apply, and synthesize clinical research, relevant to nursing and health promotion.

title: Introduction to Nursing Informatics
description: Covers topics relevant to evidence-based practice, nursing informatics as a specialty, electronic health records and clinical informatics, clinical decision support and decision analysis, using informatics to promote community/population health, telenursing and remote access telehealth, and ethical issues in nursing informatics.

title: Compassion, Communication, and Care of Underserved Populations
description: Addresses the root causes of health disparities experienced by underserved at-risk populations (e.g., the homeless, people of color, victims of violence) using a historical, sociocultural, behavioral, and personal lens.

title: Frameworks for Professional Nursing Practice
description: Focuses on the scope and standards of professional nursing practice. Topics address the professional, political, and economic contexts of nursing practice, with an emphasis on jurisprudence and ethics, professional interpersonal relationships, and nursing’s role in the care delivery system.

title: Physical Assessment
description: Focuses on the development of skills in therapeutic communication, interviewing, functional assessment across the lifespan, the art and science of human care, and clinical judgment. Materials Fee

title: Nursing Skills
description: Focuses on the development of skills in therapeutic communication, interviewing, functional assessment across the lifespan, the art and science of human care, and clinical judgment.
prerequisites_raw: NUR SCI 202 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 208 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 209A with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 219 with a minimum grade of C

title: Ph.D. Seminar: Nursing and Interdisciplinary Research to Improve Human Health
description: Students learn from interdisciplinary scientists about aspects of applied health-related research. Students are introduced to new paradigms, theories, approaches, and analytical methods in health-related research. Ph.D. Nursing Science students and Ph.D. students in other disciplines are encouraged.

title: Philosophy, Science, and Nursing: Comparisons and Critiques
description: Development of philosophy and science in relation to nursing science, scholarship, and practice; emphasis on inquiry, scientific reasoning, and contemporary philosophical thought; historical and contemporary influences on nursing science theory development; evaluation/analysis of interdisciplinary theory and application to nursing research.

title: Measurement of Health-Related Behavior
description: Provides a comprehensive understanding of psychometric principles, analyses, and emerging concepts like Intensive Longitudinal Methods to measure behavior in natural contexts using newer technologies (e.g., smartphones, wearable sensors, and Internet of Things). Students from different disciplines are encouraged.
prerequisites_raw: Recommended: a graduate-level statistics course

title: Health Promotion/Disease Prevention
description: Incorporates principles of health promotion and disease prevention to provide culturally sensitive, evidence-based care for individuals, families, and communities. Focuses on critically analyzing and integrating current prevention guidelines to develop individualized plans of care and provide holistic and integrative education.

title: Critical Thinking Through Writing Critique
description: Aims to stimulate critical thinking by using existing scientific literature to work out the structure of their arguments, evaluate their logical clarity, identify unquestioned assumptions, and link all this to the rigor/appropriateness of any inferences made.

title: Applied Pharmacology
description: Principles of pharmacology applied to intervention in pathophysiologic states across the life span. Discussion of the major drug groups with implications for monitoring, drug administration, toxicity, and patient education included. Physical, psychological, social, and cultural factors affecting drug administration.
prerequisites_raw: NUR SCI 202 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 208 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 209A with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 219 with a minimum grade of C

title: Pathophysiology
description: Focuses on pathologic alterations in physiologic processes in cells, tissues, organs, and systems across the life span. Emphasis is placed on critical thinking, application of concepts to clinical practice, and related research.

title: Medical Surgical Nursing 1
description: Focuses on the introduction of medical surgical nursing application with a focus on the older adult population. Emphasis is placed on identifying and synthesizing the unique set of factors influencing nursing management of individual older adults.
prerequisites_raw: NUR SCI 202 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 208 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 209A with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 219 with a minimum grade of C

title: Medical Surgical Nursing 2
description: Examines nursing assessment and advanced nursing management for acute and chronic health problems within the inpatient hospital setting. Theory content emphasizes assessment, health history, diagnostic reasoning, and nursing prioritization of care in medically complicated patients.
prerequisites_raw: NUR SCI 209B with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 217 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 221A with a minimum grade of C

title: Seminar in Clinical Translational Science
description: Discussion of clinical translational science methods in the context of nursing science research. Emphasis placed on interdisciplinary and community participatory research approaches.
prerequisites_raw: Consent of the instructor is required

title: Biostatistics for Health Sciences I
description: Helps students to develop skills necessary for applying statistical principles and practices in health research. This is achieved through in-depth review of existing research articles and hands-on statistical programming exercises.

title: Biostatistics for Health Sciences II
description: Introduces advanced methods of statistical analysis and research design used in health research. These include linear, logistic, Poisson regression, and a brief introduction to regression models for correlated data.
prerequisites_raw: NUR SCI 223A with a minimum grade of B-

title: Research Designs in Nursing Science
description: Provides an introduction to qualitative and quantitative research designs, methods, and analyses in nursing science. Evaluation of measurement and population issues, data management, ethics, analytical approaches, mixed methods work, and translational potential in the context of research.

title: Advanced Pharmacology II
description: Principles of pharmacology that serve as a foundation for the pharmacotherapeutic management of patients evaluated and treated by advanced practice nurses. Emphasis includes the application of pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic principles.
prerequisites_raw: NUR SCI 225A with a minimum grade of B

title: Theoretical and Conceptual Frameworks
description: Explores the history, roles, and uses of theory in nursing and health scholarship. Students examine, analyze, and utilize the components of theory, theory construction, concept analysis, and theory evaluation.

title: Grant Writing I
description: Introduction to the principles and methods of proposal writing used in preparing grant proposals. Provides content on the process for good proposal development, key elements and sections of proposal, necessary information to include in grant proposal and development of budget.
prerequisites_raw: NUR SCI 212 with a minimum grade of B- and NUR SCI 226 with a minimum grade of B-

title: Grant Writing II
description: Provides a continuation of skill building in preparing a grant proposal, with emphasis on developing the educational training plan, budget and budget justification, the IRB and ethics component, and letters of support for a career-development grant.

title: Human Behavior and Mental Health Care
description: Focuses on nursing management of individuals across the lifespan with alterations in mental health. Mental health promotion and crisis intervention, chemical dependency, acute and chronic care for psychiatric conditions, rehabilitation, and recovery are addressed.
prerequisites_raw: NUR SCI 209B with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 217 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 221A with a minimum grade of C

title: Pain: Symptoms, Science, and Treatment
description: Covers theory, assessment, experience, and management of pain.

title: Advanced Health and Physical Assessment
description: Application of theoretical concepts related to comprehensive health assessment of patients across the lifespan. Analysis, synthesis, and application of comprehensive health assessment data.

title: Advanced Health and Physical Assessment Laboratory
description: Clinical laboratory course for the application of concepts related to comprehensive health assessment of patients across the lifespan.

title: Appraisal and Translation of Evidence for Practice
description: Provides advanced concepts on research methods and measurement strategies that are applicable to support the advanced practice nurse to access, evaluate, and utilize data from various sources including research, quality improvement initiatives, and information technology origins to achieve improvements.
prerequisites_raw: Consent of the instructor is required

title: Health Politics and Policy
description: Participants analyze, apply, and evaluate current health policy-related literature, engage in the process of health policy development within professional, regulatory, or administrative environments, and develop an evidence-based health policy proposal across the spectrum of health care systems.

title: DNP Scholarly Project I: Conceptualization and Planning
description: Students gain the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to develop an evidence-based project plan and proposal. Structured didactic content and application of the Student's DNP Scholarly Project. First of four DNP Scholarly Project courses.

title: Social Determinants of Health and Health Equity
description: The four components of the Clinical Prevention and Population Health Framework: evidence-based practice, clinical preventive service and health promotion, health systems and policy, and population health and community aspects of practice with emphasis on ethical care delivery.

title: DNP Intersession
description: Provides DNP students an opportunity to present and receive faculty and peer feedback on their DNP project plan. Recommendations related to practical data collection and information gathering approaches and data analysis are also emphasized.

title: Foundations of Health Systems and Health Economics
description: Foundational understanding of how healthcare is financed in the U.S. Explores economic theories and policies, various types of healthcare organizations, and healthcare delivery systems. Healthcare finance is discussed at national and practice levels.

title: The Science of Change, Quality Improvement, and Program Evaluation
description: Intro to science of quality improvement and program evaluation. Focus on info system technology and its application in quality improvement. Focus placed on the role of the advanced practice nurse leader in developing and leading clinical quality and safety initiatives.

title: DNP Scholarly Project II: Proposal
description: Developing a full proposal that reflects synthesis of the student's knowledge from prior coursework and work in an area of interest or expertise under the direction of a faculty mentor. Second of four DNP Scholarly Project course sequence.

title: DNP Scholarly Project III: Implementation and Evaluation
description: Continued development of knowledge, skills, and abilities to implement the chosen DNP proposal. Students receive direction from a faculty mentor and peer feedback as they become engaged in the microsystem where they are implementing their DNP Scholarly Project.

title: DNP Scholarly Project IV: Implications
description: Selection and implementation of evidence-based interventions supported through informatics and technological advances and measurement of outcomes in a selected practicum site as applicable. Includes reflection and mapping of the DNP Scholarly Project with DNP Essentials as published.

title: DNP Epilogue
description: DNP students develop DNP competency through the presentation of their project and development of a professional manuscript. Individual direction from the DNP Project Team and peer feedback are provided throughout the course.

title: A Systems Approach to Health and Well-Being
description: Focuses on using a systems approach to promote individual and population wellness. The key topics include complex/dynamic system, analytic tools to measure dynamic/ interrelated processes, critical analysis of literature that utilizes the systems approach to promote holistic well-being.

title: Primary Care Adult/Gerontology Acute Common Conditions
description: Assessment and management of acute or episodic problems affecting patients and families across the lifespan. Diagnostics, pharmacology, pathophysiology, and therapeutics are integrated. Concepts of quality health care, resource management, and shared-decision making are emphasized.
prerequisites_raw: NUR SCI 210 with a minimum grade of B and NUR SCI 230 with a minimum grade of B

title: Qualitative Research Designs in Nursing Science
description: Seminar in qualitative research philosophies, methods, and analysis in nursing science clinical research. Consideration of population access and sampling, ethics, data management, analytical approaches, and translational potential.

title: Quantitative Research Designs in Nursing Science
description: Seminar in experimental and survey research designs, methods, and analysis in nursing science clinical research. Consideration of measurement issues, mixed methods models, population access and sampling, data management, analytical approaches, and translational potential.
prerequisites_raw: NUR SCI 212 with a minimum grade of B-

title: Curricular Design for the Health Professions
description: Introduces students to the theoretical foundations, essential components, and accreditation standards for curriculum development at the program level. Outcome competencies are addressed as they apply to the development and evaluation of an educational program to meet society’s diverse healthcare needs.

title: Transformational Leadership in Education for the Health Professions
description: Students are introduced to the role of the nurse educator as change agent, leader, and scholar and are provided experience in planning learner-centered learning activities that are engaging and effective in achieving desired student performance.

title: Primary Care Women's Health
description: Primary health care needs of women including adolescent, adult, and aging adults. Emphasizes assessment, diagnosis, prevention, management, and education of common gynecologic and family planning health care needs.
prerequisites_raw: NUR SCI 210 with a minimum grade of B and NUR SCI 230 with a minimum grade of B

title: Nursing Informatics
description: Provides an overview of nursing informatics topics for practice.

title: Applied Data Science for Clinical Research
description: Provides hands-on training in applied data science for clinical research.

title: Primary Care Obstetrics
description: Assessment and management of women during pregnancy. Diagnostics, pharmacology, pathophysiology and therapeutics are integrated. Includes assessment, differential diagnosis, management, patient/family education, and counseling related to normal pregnancy care.
prerequisites_raw: NUR SCI 210 with a minimum grade of B NUR SCI 230 with a minimum grade of B

title: Primary Care Adult/Gerontology Chronic Conditions
description: Assessment and management of acute or episodic problems affecting adult and geriatric patients and their families. Diagnostics, pharmacology, pathophysiology, and therapeutic are integrated.
prerequisites_raw: NUR SCI 245 with a minimum grade of B

title: Advanced Qualitative and Mixed Methods Research Design
description: Discussion and application course on design and implementation of qualitative, mixed methods research. Emphasis on data analysis and management skills, interpretation of findings, reflexivity and ethical considerations in field work, and the development of publishable products for dissemination.
prerequisites_raw: Enrollment in a UCI Ph.D. program and at least one introduction qualitative course

title: Primary Care Pediatrics
description: Assessment and management of acute or episodic problems affecting pediatric patients and their families. Diagnostics, pharmacology, pathophysiology, and therapeutics are integrated.
prerequisites_raw: NUR SCI 210 with a minimum grade of B and NUR SCI 230 with a minimum grade of B

title: Community-Based Health Care
description: Epidemiology, primary health care promotion, and disease prevention applied to nursing care of individuals, families, groups, and communities. Includes sociocultural, political, economic, and environmental influences. Concepts and methods of assessing populations and communities incorporated in concurrent practicum.
prerequisites_raw: NUR SCI 215 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 274 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 276 with a minimum grade of C

title: Pediatrics: Care of Children and Families
description: Provides didactic and clinical experiences in nursing management of infants, children, and adolescents with acute, chronic, and emergency illnesses with an emphasis on social, cultural, and developmental influences.
prerequisites_raw: NUR SCI 201 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 221B with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 228 with a minimum grade of C

title: Maternity and Women’s Health Care
description: Provides didactic and clinical experiences in nursing management of women’s wellness across the lifespan, the childbirth process, and newborn care. Incorporates concepts of family-centered care, teamwork and collaboration, patient safety, quality improvement and informatics, utilizing an evidence-based practice approach.
prerequisites_raw: NUR SCI 201 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 221B with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 228 with a minimum grade of C

title: Critical and Specialty Health Care
description: Focuses on the delivery of patient-centered care and collaborative management of individuals with actual or potential life-threatening alterations in health status. Practicum in critical care units emphasizes teamwork, collaboration, informatics, evidence-based practice, safety, and quality improvement in safe care delivery.
prerequisites_raw: NUR SCI 200 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 272 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 273 with a minimum grade of C

title: Clinical Preceptorship
description: Hybrid clinical course facilitated by nursing faculty and clinicians focusing on in-depth clinical nursing practice and preparation for transition to independent practice. Topics covering NCLEX preparation, BRN application, and professional transition activities are discussed.
prerequisites_raw: NUR SCI 215 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 274 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 276 with a minimum grade of C

title: Leadership and Management in Health Care
description: Focuses on the role of the professional nurse as leader and manager of a health team. Principles, concepts, and theories related to organizations, management, leadership, change, decision-making, and group process are applied to the delivery of health care.
prerequisites_raw: NUR SCI 200 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 272 with a minimum grade of C and NUR SCI 273 with a minimum grade of C

title: Implementation Science
description: Focuses on dissemination and implementation (D&I) science. Emphasizes the types of questions D&I research seeks to answer, commonly used models and frameworks, methods employed, and outcomes examined.

title: Frameworks for the Advanced Practice Registered Nursing Role: Nurse Practitioner
description: Orientation to the scope and standards of advanced practice registered nursing pertinent to the APRN role. Principles of jurisprudence, ethics, and advocacy will be introduced along with conceptual frameworks for advanced nursing practice.

title: Compassionate Care with Underserved Populations
description: Addresses theory/research on health risk factors (e.g., psychiatric illness, sociocultural and economic characteristics) that impact patient health and well-being across the lifespan. Emphasis is on cultural awareness, lifestyle modification, community resources, and communication/coping strategies to promote well-being.

title: Primary Care Procedures
description: Introduces the theoretical basis for common procedures performed in primary care clinical practice. Focus includes EKG interpretation, x-ray interpretation, minor surgery, and orthopaedic procedures.
prerequisites_raw: NUR SCI 245 with a minimum grade of B

title: Scholarly Concentration
description: Focuses on analysis and use of research to provide the evidence-base nursing practice in an area of interest. Students critique, synthesize, and analyze a body of clinical and behavioral research evidence.
prerequisites_raw: NUR SCI 200 with a minimum grade of C

title: DNP APRN Practicum I
description: Clinical application of theory and research related to the advanced assessment and health promotion of patients across the lifespan.
prerequisites_raw: NUR SCI 210 with a minimum grade of B and NUR SCI 230 with a minimum grade of B and ( NUR SCI 230L with a minimum grade of B or NUR SCI 231L with a minimum grade of B)
